articles.title: Austen is for everyone: Sense and Sensibility (2026)
articles.description: Like a warm beverage on a crisp autumn evening, Georgia Oakley's Sense and Sensibility (2026) is the perfect girls-night-in film as the temperature drops here in Baltimore. While some Austen purists may be clutching their pearls, as a casual Austen fan I had a wonderful time with the newest adaptation of the classic novel. This movie captures her characteristic wit and charm and brings it to the modern era of cinema. The 1811 novel centers around the Dashwood family, particularly the romantic entanglements of the eldest daughters Elinor (Daisy Edgar-Jones) and Marianne (Esmé Creed-Miles), as they deal with their newfound financial difficulties after the death of their father. Elinor, the eldest represents sense with her endless pragmatism and restraint, and Marianne represents sensibility with her intense passion and romantic idealism. While the story follows each of their romances, an argument can be made that the real love story is that of Elinor and Marianne - something Oakley highlights. Throughout the novel, Marianne grows to have a bit more sense and Elinor becomes a bit more sensible. The film is rooted in its characters, and both actresses make for deeply personable leads. I knew going in that Edgar-Jones (of Normal People fame) would capture the audience's attention, but Creed-Miles fully holds her own as the wild, tempestuous Marianne. George MacKay is also the perfect choice for Edward, Elinor's love interest. With a piercing gaze and incredibly English features (in The-Year-of-Zendaya/Robert Pattinson/Anne Hathaway, I'm so grateful I've never seen his face before), he delivers the yearning now mandatory for a romance. Fiona Shaw also steals the show as the endlessly prattling Mrs. Jennings. She turns what I had expected to be a strictly comedic-relief role into a memorably endearing one. Everyone is familiar with the 2005 Pride and Prejudice (if you haven't seen the film, you've definitely seen a clip of the Darcy hand-flex); among Austen fans, the 1995 Sense and Sensibility film starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet is truly beloved (not to mention its 7 Academy Award nominations and win for Best Adapted Screenplay), so Oakley had big shoes to fill. She took visual inspiration from the 2005 classic, with rich sepia tones and vast natural landscapes, but made it her own with some interesting parallel compositions. In the era of remakes, the film is an adaptation done right, with changes to the plot only in service of the greater story (Wuthering Heights, I'm looking at you). The reason these stories remain so popular is that they tackle universal themes of sisterhood, romantic misunderstanding and integrity, and they do not need significant adjusting in order to be relatable to modern audiences. Elinor has a grand romantic moment running after Edward to clarify a misunderstanding, which never happened in the book, but is a neat way to conclude her arc as a person learning to express her feelings. Edward was also made much more likeable in this iteration than the 1995 version (what can I say, Hugh Grant doesn't do it for me), which helps us root for our main leads. While the script is not the most subtle in its wit, it is a homage to Austen's famously biting and clever dialogue which left me laughing all the way through. Unfortunately, the duel scene between Brandon and Willoughby (Marianne's love interests) near the end felt off both in tone and in score, likely because this happened off-page in the book. Also, try as I might to ignore it, I did find Marianne's unkempt hair distractedly disheveled at times. As on-brand for her character as it was, it seemed odd because the rest of the film seems to capture the 18th century so well (aside from the dances, for which I'll defer to an expert). There has been some discourse about historical accuracy in these period pieces (see: Bridgerton). While this one is definitely not perfect, as she discusses in this interview with IndieWire, costume designer Grace Snell highlights how the two sisters learn from one another in the way they dress over the course of the story: Elinor with more ribbons and Marianne with more structure. Oakley's choices were in service to her characters rather than the time period, and as a casual viewer, I'd say it worked. Sense and Sensibility wasn't a life-changing film, nor do I see it winning an Academy Award like its predecessor, but it was a cozy one - warm and easy and comforting in all the right ways - and definitely worth watching whenever it comes to streaming, regardless of your familiarity with the source material.

articles.title: Ways to Stay Healthy This Flu Season
articles.description: Happy autumn, Blue Jays! While the leaves falling down and the chillier weather are exciting, this is also a time where many students get sick. Whether it be a fever, headache, or sore throat, catching an illness is not a fun time. To try and avoid this, here are a few tips from me on how to not get sick and how to recover quickly if you do. To prevent sickness: 1) Drink water Sounds cliche, I know. But the #1 thing you can do, in my opinion, to stay healthy is consume lots of fluids, preferably room temperature or heated. Drinking water has SO many benefits, and it's free. a. Kidney health Trust me, you want your kidneys to be healthy no matter what. Kidney stones are about the most painful things you can experience. b. Metabolism Fills up your stomach and helps regulate your metabolism and temperature. Water prevents overeating and maintains balance of body fluids. c. Skin health Drinking water keeps your skin looking glowy and soft. d. Digestion Feeling bloated? Drink hot water! This acts as a lubricant for your organs and heats you up from the inside. e. Keeps you warm Drinking warm or hot water combats the cold weather. This in itself keeps you from getting sick. 2) Layer up Remember when you were a kid and your mom always told you to bring an extra jacket? This might've been annoying at the time, but she was right. It's always a good idea to layer up, and it's much better to err on the side of too hot instead of too cold. You can always remove layers but you can't add them if you didn't bring them! Some ways to do this are: - Layering leggings underneath baggy jeans - Layering long sleeves or turtlenecks underneath sweaters, crewnecks, or hoodies - Always bringing an extra jacket 3) Get enough sleep I'm lucky enough to be in Introduction to Psychology (shoutout Chaz Firestone the goat), and this past week we learned about the vast importance of sleep. In fact, sleep is more effective for concentration than caffeine and the abuse of stimulants such as Adderall. Getting enough sleep helps your immune system because it gives it enough energy to fight a potential illness. Feeling happier and more well rested after sleep can also improve overall health. If you do get sick, here are some ways to ensure a speedy recovery: 1) Drink ginger tea!! This was a tip made by my mom, who always made this whenever my siblings and I got sick. She would boil cut up ginger with water, and we would drink the spicy concoction, bundle up and fall asleep sweating. Although this sounds odd, it has always worked. I don't know how feasible this is in a dorm room, although it's possible that Charles Street Market sells ginger. 2) Gargle salt water This tip works best if you have a sore throat. Have you ever woken up and swallowed and it hurt? Terrible experience. Mix about 1 teaspoon of salt into warm water and gargle for 30-60 seconds for temporary relief. 3) Bundle up Always dress more heavily than you should. Sweating helps the illness go away, and staying warm is a top priority. Do not go outside with wet hair, and try to cover your body with hats (like a beanie) and scarves or turtlenecks. Wear gloves and long socks as well. Please take care of yourselves!! Remember, your health is always a top priority over anything else. If you feel something is wrong, get it checked out before it is too late. There are plenty of free resources provided to you on campus that are waiting to be utilized. I hope these tips are helpful, and I wish you guys the best of luck this flu season.

Globally, an estimated 4.5 trillion cigarette butts are discarded annually, making them the most common type of litter on beaches over the past three decades.

articles.title: White Dwarfs Are Actually…Yellow, Green, Pink, and Purple?
articles.description: The universe hosts a myriad of star types, including supergiants, giants, main sequence, red dwarfs, brown dwarfs, white dwarfs, and neutron stars. What makes these stars stand out are just their sizes, but their colors, as each one hosts a distinct color based on their surface temperature, specifically orange, red, blue, and white based on cooler to hotter temperatures. While the correlation between star colors and surface temperatures has long been known throughout astronomy, what if star colors could change based on specific criteria, including their atmosphere?

Solutions to mitigate biodiversity loss depend on the answer to this question.

articles.title: Bacteria reinvent their weapons through selection, chance and gene swapping
articles.description: Many of the most potent antibiotics originate from bacteria. A large proportion belong to a class of compounds known as nonribosomal peptides (NRP). They are produced by large bacterial enzyme machineries—the nonribosomal peptide synthetases, or NRPS for short. These function like molecular assembly lines: Similar to the stations in a car factory, where new parts are added to the car at each step, several specialized modules string together amino acid by amino acid to build a peptide.
